title: Moses as prophet of future figures
english: We receive Moses as a prophet. He wrote down figures of things that were to come. Whoever holds only the letter does not recognize the prophet.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is concluding the homily, stating the principle that Moses wrote figures of future things and that only a spiritual reader recognizes him as a prophet.

title: After the golden calf: multiplied sacrifices as medicine for pride; the law as tutor to Christ
english: After the golden calf, the sacrifices were multiplied as a medicine for pride. The law is a tutor toward Christ.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining why the Levitical sacrifices were multiplied after Israel's sin with the golden calf, and how the law functioned as a tutor leading to Christ.

title: The two goats as a mystery of Christ
english: Two goats: one lot for the Lord, and one lot for the one sent away (Leviticus 16:8). One is sacrificed, the other is sent away. Each is a mystery of Christ.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Day of Atonement ritual from Leviticus, where two goats are chosen by lot, one for the Lord and one for the scapegoat.

title: The prepared and clean man leads the goat into the desert
english: A prepared and clean man leads the goat into the desert (Leviticus 16:21). This is the ministry of the apostles. Cleanliness is required for the mystery.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Day of Atonement ritual of the scapegoat, identifying the man who leads it away as a figure of the apostles' ministry.

title: The catechumen's cleansing and baptism
english: It can also be understood another way: a cleansed catechumen leads his sins far away. Baptism sends them into the desert.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the scapegoat ritual of Leviticus 16, applying it to the catechumen and baptism.

title: The lot is God's providence, not blind chance
english: The lot is not blind chance; it is the providence of God. The lots are apostolic. The Lord disposes.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the meaning of the lot in the Levitical rite, after discussing how baptism sends sins into the desert.

title: Christ alone enters the true holy place
english: The high priest takes some of the blood and carries it within the veil (Leviticus 16:15). Christ alone enters the true holy things.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the high priest's entry into the holy place on the Day of Atonement as a figure of Christ's unique entry into the true sanctuary.

title: Prayer as burning coals and incense
english: A censer full of coals is prayer burning. Incense upon the fire. Prayer ascends.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the high priest's entry with the censer and incense on the Day of Atonement as a figure of prayer.

title: The cloud of incense veils the mercy seat
english: Let a cloud of incense cover the mercy seat (Leviticus 16:13). Glory hidden. Fear to approach naked.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the high priest's incense ritual on the Day of Atonement, applying it to prayer and the hidden glory of God.

title: Incense on the fire before the Lord
english: He will place the incense on the fire before the Lord (Leviticus 16:13). Fire tests. Pure prayer.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the high priest's ritual of putting incense on the fire in the tabernacle, applying it to the soul's prayer.

title: The High Priest Enters Alone
english: No one will be in the tabernacle when the high priest enters (Leviticus 16:17). He is the only mediator. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is closing the homily by applying the Day of Atonement rite, where the high priest enters the tabernacle alone, to Christ as the sole mediator.
